message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds any portion. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.). | • Report problems in writing (email or certified mail).
• If the landlord fails to fix, you may withhold rent, repair and deduct, or file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease and not excessive. | • Keep receipts or bank records. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month**: Either party may terminate with **30 days’ written notice**.
• **Fixed‑term**: The lease ends automatically unless renewed. | • Provide written notice (email or certified mail) at least 30 days before the end of the term. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries; if the landlord enters without notice, you can file a complaint. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, provided you follow the proper procedure. | • Document the issue, send a written notice, keep receipts, and give the landlord a chance to fix before deducting. | | **Eviction Process** | • The landlord must provide a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violations, 60 days for no‑cause termination).
• Eviction must go through the court; the landlord cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond to notices promptly; seek legal counsel if you believe the eviction is unlawful. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report disturbances; if unresolved, consider mediation or legal action. | | **Fair Housing** | • Texas law protects against discrimination in housing. | • File complaints with TCHR or HUD if you suspect discrimination. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify who pays utilities. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease; dispute charges if necessary. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Generally requires landlord’s written consent unless the lease allows it. | • Obtain written permission; keep copies. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must maintain common areas (hallways, elevators, etc.) in a safe condition. | • Report issues; if ignored, you may file a complaint. | | **Legal Remedies** | • You can sue for breach of contract, damages, or seek a court order to compel repairs. | • Consider small claims court for amounts under $20,000. | #### Quick Tips 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Many rights are spelled out in the lease; if something seems unfair, ask for clarification or negotiate before signing. 2. **Keep Records** – Written notices, emails, photos, and receipts are your best evidence if disputes arise. 3. **Know the Timeline** – Texas law sets specific notice periods for entry, rent increases, and termination; staying ahead of deadlines protects you. 4. **Seek Help Early** – If you’re facing a problem, contact the TDHCA, TCHR, or a local tenant advocacy group before the situation escalates. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant rights organization.
